extraction.summary: A 74-year-old male with a history of CKD stage 3b, atrial fibrillation on anticoagulation, prostate cancer, and recurrent UTIs presented to the ED via ambulance with acute confusion, reduced oral intake, and slurred speech. Vital signs demonstrate severe systemic inflammatory response and shock with hyperthermia (38.9 C), tachycardia (124 bpm), tachypnea (28 bpm), hypotension (88/52 mmHg), hypoxia (SpO2 90% on 6 L/min O2), and altered mental status (AVPU V). Bedside lab evaluation reveals severe hyperlactatemia (4.8 mmol/L), acute renal impairment (creatinine 218 umol/L), marked leukocytosis (WBC 17.2 x10^9/L), and elevated CRP (187 mg/L). Sepsis Six protocols have been initiated for suspected urosepsis, with medical registrar and critical care outreach teams requested.
extraction.clinical_reasoning: This patient's document drives severe clinical concern for septic shock secondary to suspected urosepsis. This is driven by physiological instability including hyperthermia (38.9 C), sinus tachycardia (124 bpm), tachypnea (28 bpm), hypotension (88/52 mmHg), peripheral hypoperfusion (4 sec cap refill, cool/mottled peripheries), oliguria (15 mL/hr), elevated BM (14.2 mmol/L), and altered sensorium (responds to voice only). Bedside labs support severe systemic infection and acute organ dysfunction with critical hyperlactatemia (4.8 mmol/L), elevated inflammatory markers (WBC 17.2 x10^9/L, CRP 187 mg/L), and severe kidney injury (creatinine 218 umol/L, urea 19.4 mmol/L). His background of prostate cancer and 3 UTIs in 8 months strongly points to a urinary origin.
recommended_next_steps: Immediate evaluation by medical registrar and critical care outreach team.
Continue aggressive fluid resuscitation for persistent hypotension and septic shock.
Repeat bedside blood lactate to assess clearance and therapeutic response.
Monitor hourly urinary output via catheter.
Perform CT abdomen as requested once hemodynamically stabilized.
Follow up formal laboratory blood results and blood/urine cultures.
Verify home medications against community pharmacy records and clarify allergy status.
